description: The Raffles City Italian hit from chef Antonio Miscellaneo opened its third outlet at Tampines Mall on 15 May 2026. Everything is made from scratch and nothing on the menu tops S$30 — the crab tagliatelle (S$26) and margherita (S$17) are the signatures. The Tampines outlet gets six exclusive dishes, including a smoked-provola margherita affumicata (S$19) and seabass-stuffed agnolotti with Argentinean prawns (S$27).
parking: Tampines Mall multi-storey carpark; Tampines MRT is right outside.
title: Casa Vostra — viral Italian finally lands in Tampines
why: Six Tampines-exclusive dishes you can't get at the town outlets — easties skip the Raffles City queues.

description: Opened 2 Sep 2026 on Tampines Mall's fourth floor, Im Qalb is the Thai-Malay offshoot of Vincent Pang's Im Jai, run by the ex-hedge-fund chef who trained at Le Cordon Bleu Dusit in Bangkok. The menu leans into southern Thai cooking with Malay influences: golden crab tahu kai jeow (S$18.80), stir-fried squid in black ink sauce (S$19.80), and southern Thai-style ayam perchik skewers (S$18.80). It's working towards halal certification.
parking: Tampines Mall multi-storey carpark; Tampines MRT is right outside.
title: Im Qalb — brand-new Thai-Malay kitchen in Tampines
why: Opened 2 Sep 2026 — one of the freshest openings in the heartlands this week.

description: Chef Joel Ong's third concept is a retro-styled cafe in a Tampines HDB block serving elevated Nanyang comfort food. The draw is the nasi lemak sets — pork belly berempah (S$14.90) or fried chicken berempah (S$12.90) with a choice of coconut rice or Indomie, the meats marinated over two days. Kaya butter toast (S$2.90) and Heartland laksa (S$14.90) round out the menu. It stays open until 2am daily, a rarity for supper in the east.
parking: HDB carpark at Block 481; limited at peak hours, so public transport is easier.
title: Heartland by Enjoy — retro Nanyang supper till 2am
why: A genuine late-night option in the heartlands — kitchens open till 2am every day.

description: Burma Social's Siglap outlet blends Burmese, Thai, Indian, Chinese and Laotian flavours in a contemporary shophouse setting. On weekends, order any main (S$28 for one, S$38 for two) and unlock 90 minutes of unlimited momos and samosas — the signature Burmese noodles and mala veg wok are the mains to beat. A boozy upgrade (S$49) adds two hours of free-flow Asahi, prosecco, wine and spirits.
parking: Limited street parking on East Coast Road; buses 13/16 or Marine Terrace MRT plus a short bus ride.
title: Burma Social — bottomless brunch in Siglap
when: Wed-Sun 11:30am-3pm; dinner Tue-Sun 6pm-11pm (Fri-Sat till 12am); closed Mon
why: The weekend bottomless brunch (free-flow momos and samosas) is the best-value leisurely lunch on the East Coast.

description: Singapore's newest hawker centre opened 25 Jul 2025 in Punggol Digital District with 40 stalls and 576 seats, run cashless with AI-assisted queue management. The lineup mixes heritage and hype: Michelin Bib Gourmand Singapore Fried Hokkien Mee, the revived 50-year-old South Buona Vista Braised Duck, Hock Hai (Hong Lim) Curry Chicken, plus Gen-Z stalls like What The Puff! curry puffs (from S$2). Kopi-O and teh-O go for S$1.
parking: Carpark at the hawker centre / Punggol Coast Mall; steps from Punggol Coast MRT (NEL).
title: Punggol Coast Hawker Centre — 40 stalls, Michelin names
why: The northeast's flagship new food centre — heritage stalls and young hawkers under one roof, most dishes under S$10.

description: South Korea's largest fried chicken chain (1,400+ outlets) is back in Singapore after shutting all local stores in 2022, now at 18 Cross in the CBD. The headline order is the SuperThigh Chicken Burger (S$9.95) built on a boneless fried thigh, plus Boneless Fried Chicken Thigh (from S$9.95) in four flavours including soy garlic and cheesy Sichuan. Open daily 7am-10pm, so it doubles as a breakfast-to-supper option.
parking: Limited parking around 18 Cross; Tanjong Pagar or Telok Ayer MRT are minutes away.
title: Mom's Touch — Korea's fried-chicken giant returns
why: The comeback story of the month — Korea's biggest chicken chain returns to Singapore after four years away.

description: At OUE Downtown 2, Katsu by Kyu is Singapore's first restaurant dedicated entirely to Jeju pork tonkatsu. Cutlets go through a 10-day dry-age, are finished over rice-straw charcoal for a smoky aroma, and fried to order in crisp panko. Pick from Central Cut Premium Loin (S$42++), Loin (S$32++) or Tenderloin (S$30++), each with rice milled from Incheon, Korea — or the Tenderloin and Kadaif Prawn combo (S$32++).
parking: OUE Downtown basement parking; Tanjong Pagar MRT is the closest.
title: Katsu by Kyu — SG's first Jeju pork tonkatsu
why: A genuine first for Singapore — Jeju pork tonkatsu with 10-day dry-ageing, new in August 2026.

address: 252 North Bridge Road, Raffles City, Singapore 179103
description: The Michelin-approved unagi chain with 90 years of history has opened its second Singapore outlet at Raffles City, helmed by fourth-generation master Kikukawa Yuhei. Whole eels are filleted and grilled over binchotan for crisp skin and tender flesh. The classic Kabayaki Ippon Unagi Set (S$48++) comes with nori, pickles and eel liver soup; the Shirayaki version (S$48++) serves the eel with just salt so the char speaks for itself.
parking: Raffles City carpark; directly above City Hall MRT.
title: Unagi Yondaime Kikukawa — 90-year-old unagi masters at Raffles City
when: Hours TBC — check before heading down
why: New September 2026 opening — a 90-year-old Japanese unagi institution, now in the heart of town.

description: New on Mohamed Sultan Road, the 65-seat NOOR channels Mediterranean sharing plates — tahini, labneh, harissa — with quiet Japanese influences, led by chef Titus Thamil. Start with the tahini-slicked Shok Bread (S$16++), then Hamachi Tartlet (S$18++) in a crisp gyoza shell, finishing with Labneh Cheesecake (S$18++). Behind the main room sits a hidden 10-seat izakaya, and Thursday nights run Yalla Tokyo omakase dinners (S$88++) with live drums.
parking: Limited street parking on Mohamed Sultan Road; nearest MRT is Fort Canning or Clarke Quay, then a short walk.
title: NOOR — Mediterranean plates + hidden izakaya
why: September 2026 newcomer — Mediterranean-Japanese plates plus a secret izakaya and theatrical Thursday omakase nights.

address: 80 Marine Parade Road, #01-10, Parkway Parade, Singapore 449269
description: Michelin-starred-pedigree Sushidan opened its second Singapore outlet at Parkway Parade on 5 Sep 2026, bringing chef Hiroyuki Sato's Toyosu Market-sourced seafood to the East. The Goshoku Set (S$19.90++) is an entry-level omakase with chawanmushi, three mini dons and a sushi platter — remarkable value. From 5 to 30 Sep, add 30g of Hokkaido nama uni to any omakase course for S$18.80++.
parking: Parkway Parade carpark; Marine Parade MRT (TEL) is the nearest, or buses along Marine Parade Road.
title: Sushidan — $19.90 omakase at Parkway Parade
why: Opened 5 Sep — east-coast omakase from S$19.90++, plus a limited uni add-on running through 30 Sep.

title: Jin Le Claypot Rice — the north's claypot institution
description: The Woodlands claypot name regulars swear by: claypot chicken rice (S$6 nett) with a generous slab of salted fish, and the gongbao frog leg (S$14 nett) in a punchy oyster-sauce gravy with chilli padi heat. Burpple reviewers call the sauce 'much much better than most' and note one pot comfortably feeds two. 4.3 stars across 140+ Google reviews.
parking: HDB carpark at Blk 111; a short walk from Woodlands MRT.
why: Gongbao frog leg and claypot rice in the heart of Woodlands - the north finally gets its food-tab spotlight.

title: Ivan's Carbina — Swiss rösti in a Woodlands kopitiam
description: A Woodlands original for over a decade: a humble kopitiam stall doing crisp Swiss-style rösti — crackly golden crust, soft buttery middle — paired with chicken chop (S$7.80), snail pork sausage (S$11) or a carbonara (S$5.50). Sour cream with a lemon lift comes on the side. Eatbook's verdict: decent Western food for cheap prices, worth the trip if you're in the neighbourhood. 4.2 stars from 600+ Google reviews.
address: 354A Woodlands Avenue 5, #01-01, Lucky Star Coffeeshop, Singapore 730354
parking: Street parking near Lucky Star Coffeeshop; about 6 min on foot from Woodlands MRT.
why: Crisp rösti at kopitiam prices — a Woodlands institution for more than ten years.

title: Yan Ji Seafood Soup — 40 years of rich broth in Marsiling
description: A 40-year-old family brand at Marsiling Mall Hawker Centre: broth slow-cooked up to six hours with old hen, pork ribs, Chinese ham and Japanese scallops. The Straits Times singled out the minced pork — pounded with toasted dried sole fish for deep umami. Bowls from S$7.50 (dory) to S$18 (crayfish); braised pig trotters (S$7) for the adventurous.
address: 4 Woodlands Street 12, #01-26, Marsiling Mall Hawker Centre, Singapore 738623
parking: Marsiling Mall hawker centre; Marsiling MRT is minutes away on foot.
why: A 40-year-old seafood soup institution — the dried-sole minced pork is the order.
